error.file:json: The file is not a JSON file.
error.file:format: The file is not a mission file of this application.
error.file:version: The mission file has a version that this application cannot read.
error.file:plan: The plan in the mission file is incorrect.
error.file:spacecraft: The spacecraft data in the mission file is incorrect.
error.file:flight: The flight in the mission file is incorrect.

mission.title: Mission
mission.intro: A mission has a plan (patched conics) and a flight (trajectory in the full force model). The two modes of the application use the same mission.
mission.startNote: A new mission starts with a transfer from the Earth to Mars. You change the sequence of bodies on the Flyby tour screen.
mission.libraryNote: The browser keeps the saved missions on this computer. The application sends no data to a server.
mission.actualNote: The application calculates each actual mission again in your browser. The inputs are the launch time, the bodies and the dates of the encounters, and the aim point at the last body. Each path is a result of the engine: the application has no stored trajectory.
mission.massNote: The mass values and the specific impulse are example values. Change them to the values of your spacecraft. The trajectory does not use them.
mission.massNoteActual: The mass values and the specific impulse are example values. They are not the values of the actual spacecraft.
mission.staleNote: The plan changed after the last flight calculation. The flight on this screen is the flight of the old plan. Calculate the flight again.
mission.noFlight: This mission has no flight. Calculate the flight to get the trajectory in the full force model.

failure.inside-body: The propagation stopped: the path went into a body.
failure.not-finite: The propagation stopped: a value was not a finite number.
failure.step-limit: The propagation stopped at the limit of the number of steps.

mission.notConverged: The flight calculation did not converge at all encounters. Refer to the solver details.

origins.import: From a file or a state vector

mission.launchChange: Change of the departure v∞ from the plan
mission.planVsFlightNote: Click a row to set the time of the view to the encounter. The v∞ of the flight is the v∞ of the approach hyperbola.
mission.solverNote: Stage A: the solver aims one control at the B-plane point and the periapsis time of the next body. The control is the launch velocity, a correction maneuver or a deep-space maneuver. Stage B: the solver changes the control before a flyby to make the correction after the flyby as small as possible. Stage C: the solver moves the aim point of the flyby before a deep-space maneuver. The error of the stages A and B has no unit: the limit is 1. The value of stage C is the Δv that stays.
mission.actualCompare: Comparison with the actual flight of {name}
mission.timeDiff: Time after the actual closest approach
mission.actualInputs: The dates of the encounters and the aim point at the last body are inputs. The radius at each flyby before the last body and each v∞ are results.
mission.noteApproach: Values of the approach hyperbola some time before the periapsis (the actual spacecraft did a maneuver near the body).
mission.noteAim: The aim point at this body is an input, thus the radius is not a result.

event.impact: Arrival at the surface or in the atmosphere of {body}

mission.eventsNote: Click a row to set the time of the view to the event.
